title: Persist writer deep-clones every metadata collection under StateInner each tick (state_inner.rs:1121 held 1954 ms; collect 2106 ms of a 2254 ms tick)
outcome: A persist tick's locked collect phase no longer deep-clones metadata collections that did not change since the watermark. It captures only changed metadata units, reusing the existing w-cce8 metadata-unit model and change stamps, so the StateInner hold per tick no longer scales with accumulated history (test-run cards, registrations, observations, compacted runs, waits, Engram naming, journal and audit history, sightings, layouts). Persisted bytes, ordering, watermark and crash semantics are unchanged.
acceptance: A note quantifies, from host-API persistence diagnostics and source (no live-store reads), which metadata collections dominate the collect-phase hold on the current central host, and confirms or refutes that PersistedState::metadata_from_inner (persisted_state.rs:102-144), called from collect_persist_delta_plan (state_inner.rs:698) under persist_collect_locked, is the dominant cost.

Deterministic tests show that a persist tick with N unchanged metadata collections and one changed one clones only the changed unit under StateInner (verified by the existing persist observer or a test seam, not a timing threshold), and that the persisted SQLite metadata units, watermark, predecessor and recovery behavior are byte-for-byte unchanged against the current owner; it reuses the existing metadata-unit codec and change tracking, with no new cache or parallel persistence path.

A review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher and one complete READY goes to Merger2; the post-landing live observation of the collect-phase hold is recorded under w-7bc33299e17a, not claimed here.
